newsitem.title: USA: Marathon says shuts crude, natgas in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Marathon says shuts crude, natgas in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: USX-Marathon Group said Monday it cut crude oil and natural gas production in the U.S. Gulf due to the approach of Tropical Storm Josephine.
"We shut in production yesterday afternoon because of the storm," Bill Ryder, spokesman for the company said.
About 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and 150 million gross cubic feet of natural gas were shut-in after nine fields were closed.
The fields are expected to reopen shortly, Ryder said.
Marathon's personnel have been evacuated from offshore oil platforms as a precautionary measure ahead of the storm.
Ryder added that refining capacity as its U.S. Gulf facilities had not been affected by the temporary loss of crude oil production.
Tropical Storm Josephine was seen gaining strength in the Gulf of Mexico where it was located 340 miles southwest of Apalachicola, Fla. Maximum winds are near 50 miles an hour.
